faq.a: Resources are the things used to make goods and services: land and nature, workers, machines and tools, plus time and money.
asks: What does resources mean in economics?

faq.a: Scarcity means there is not enough of something to satisfy everyone's wants. Because resources are limited, people have to make choices.

faq.q: Why do rare things cost more?
faq.a: When something is scarce and many people want it, buyers compete for it, so sellers can charge more. Gold, saffron and concert tickets are good examples.

faq.q: Is scarcity the same as poverty?
faq.a: No. Scarcity affects everyone, rich or poor, because even the richest person has only 24 hours a day. Poverty means not having enough to meet basic needs.
asks: Are rich people affected by scarcity?

faq.a: Probably not completely, because people keep wanting new things. But new technology can make some things much less scarce, like books once printing was invented.
asks: Will we ever have enough of everything?

facts: It takes roughly 150,000 crocus flowers to make one kilogram of saffron.
Economics is often described as the study of how people use limited resources to meet unlimited wants.
